title: Burpees for Beginners: A No-Jump Version That's Kinder on Your Joints
intro: The burpee is a full-body exercise that combines a squat, a plank and standing up. This beginner version has no jumping, so it's easier to control and suits small spaces.
muscles: Full body: thighs, glutes, abs, chest, shoulders and arms. It also trains heart stamina.
steps: Squat down and place both hands on the floor, in front of your feet.
Step your feet back one at a time into a plank position.
Step your feet forward one at a time, back into the squat position.
Stand tall again. That's one rep.
mistakes: Hips sagging during the plank. Tighten your tummy so your body stays straight.
Rounding your back on the way down. Bend your knees and push your hips back.
Chasing numbers until your form gets sloppy. Quality matters more than speed.
easier: Put your hands on a sturdy sofa, table or stair step so you don't have to go all the way to the floor.
harder: Jump your feet back and forward, add one push-up in the plank position, or add a small jump at the end.
dose: Beginner: 3 sets x 5-8 reps, rest 60 seconds. Do it 2 times a week, can be part of a circuit with other exercises.
safety: Stop if you feel dizzy getting up from the floor, have chest pain, or back and knee pain. If you have high blood pressure, heart problems or just gave birth, get your doctor's advice first.

faq.q: I get breathless fast doing burpees. Normal?
faq.a: Normal, because it uses your whole body. Reduce the reps, rest longer, and go slowly. Your stamina will improve with consistent training.

faq.q: Why do I feel dizzy after a few burpees?
faq.a: Maybe because you're getting up too fast from the floor. Get up slowly and breathe steadily. If the dizziness keeps happening, stop and see a doctor.

faq.q: How long before I can do full burpees with a jump?
faq.a: It's different for everyone. Once you can do 3 sets x 10 of the step version comfortably with neat form, try adding the jump little by little.
